note: Geography round 1 (part B): human geography (population, migration, settlement, urbanisation, agriculture, mining and power, manufacturing, transport, trade and tourism), regional geography of Nigeria (location, relief, drainage, climate, vegetation, population, agriculture, minerals, industry, transport, trade, regions) and ECOWAS - with population, export and density tables and a settlement case as passages.

passages.title: Population of District Z
passages.text:
The table gives the population of District
Z, which has a land area of 500 km².

Year   Population
2006     200,000
2016     260,000
2026     338,000

In 2026 the district recorded 12,000
births and 4,000 deaths. 40% of the
population was under 15 years of age and
5% was 65 years and above.

passages.title: Exports of Country K
passages.text:
The table shows the value of the exports
of Country K in 2025 (₦ billion).

Commodity      Value
Crude oil      3,600
Cocoa            400
Natural gas    1,200
Others           800
Total          6,000

In the same year the country imported
goods worth ₦7,500 billion, mostly
machinery, refined fuel and food.

passages.title: Villages of the Oke plain
passages.text: On the Oke plain, most villages are compact clusters of houses built round a central market and a chief's compound, each surrounded by farmland. Towards the hills, homesteads are scattered, each family living beside its own farm. Along the tarred road that crosses the plain, houses stand in a single line on both sides of the road for several kilometres. Two of the villages have grown into towns since a railway station and a cement factory were sited near them.

passages.title: Population density of four Nigerian states
passages.text:
The table gives the estimated population
and land area of four states.

State   Population   Area (km²)
P       9,000,000        3,600
Q       4,800,000       24,000
R       6,000,000       75,000
S       2,000,000       40,000

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The population density of District Z in 2026 was
questions.explanation: Density = population ÷ area = 338,000 ÷ 500 = 676 persons per km².

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The percentage increase in the population of District Z between 2006 and 2026 was

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The crude birth rate of District Z in 2026 was approximately
questions.explanation: Crude birth rate = births ÷ population × 1,000 = 12,000 ÷ 338,000 × 1,000 ≈ 35.5, about 36 per thousand.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The rate of natural increase of District Z in 2026 was about
questions.explanation: Natural increase = births − deaths = 8,000; 8,000 ÷ 338,000 × 100 ≈ 2.4% per annum.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The dependency ratio of District Z in 2026 (dependants per 100 workers) was approximately
questions.explanation: Dependants = 40% + 5% = 45%; working-age = 55%; ratio = 45 ÷ 55 × 100 ≈ 82.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The age structure of District Z suggests that it is
questions.A: a developed region with an ageing population
questions.B: a region where the death rate exceeds the birth rate
questions.C: a region of heavy out-migration of children
questions.D: a developing region with a youthful population and high fertility
questions.explanation: Forty per cent under 15 and only 5% elderly give a broad-based population pyramid typical of developing countries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: If the district's population continues to grow at the 2016–2026 rate, its population in 2036 will be about

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The percentage of Country K's export earnings that came from crude oil was

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The balance of trade of Country K in 2025 was
questions.explanation: Exports (6,000) − imports (7,500) = −1,500, an unfavourable balance of ₦1,500 billion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a pie chart of the exports, the sector for natural gas would measure

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The export structure of Country K shows that its economy
questions.C: depends heavily on primary products, especially oil
questions.explanation: Crude oil and gas alone make up 80% of exports and cocoa a further 6.7%; almost nothing is manufactured.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A sharp fall in world oil prices would most likely affect Country K by
questions.A: raising its export earnings and government revenue
questions.B: eliminating its trade deficit within the same year
questions.C: increasing the value of its cocoa and gas exports
questions.D: reducing foreign exchange earnings and government revenue
questions.explanation: With 60% of exports in crude oil, a price fall cuts earnings sharply, widening the deficit; this is the danger of a mono-product economy such as Nigeria's.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The percentage of export earnings from cocoa, to one decimal place, was

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The villages built as compact clusters round a market on the Oke plain have a
questions.explanation: Nucleated settlements have houses grouped closely together, usually round a focal point such as a market, church or chief's compound.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The scattered homesteads towards the hills illustrate a
questions.explanation: In a dispersed pattern individual farmsteads are separated by their fields, as in Tiv country and parts of the Middle Belt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The houses strung along the tarred road form a
questions.explanation: Linear settlements follow a road, river, canal or coastline.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The growth of two villages into towns is best explained by the
questions.A: presence of a large central market in each of the two villages
questions.B: scattering of homesteads across the farmland towards the hills
questions.C: siting of a railway station and a factory, which attracted workers and services
questions.D: fertility of the soils of the plain, which attracted more farmers
questions.explanation: New transport and industrial functions create jobs and draw in migrants, and the settlements grow in size and functions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors is most likely responsible for the nucleated villages on the plain?
questions.A: shortage of water and need for defence and cooperation
questions.B: abundance of water everywhere on the plain
questions.explanation: People cluster round a shared water source, for security and for communal farming; scattered settlement is easier where water is available everywhere.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The settlements on the Oke plain that provide goods and services to the surrounding villages are called
questions.explanation: In Christaller's theory a central place serves a surrounding trade area (hinterland) with goods and services.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The population density of State P is

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The state with the lowest population density is
questions.explanation: Densities: P 2,500; Q 200; R 80; S 50 persons per km². State S has the fewest people per square kilometre.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: State P is most probably
questions.A: a large state in the sparsely peopled Middle Belt
questions.D: a small, highly urbanised state such as Lagos
questions.explanation: A density of 2,500 per km² on only 3,600 km² matches Lagos State, Nigeria's smallest but most densely peopled state.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The combined population density of States R and S is approximately

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A choropleth map of the four states would show
questions.A: State S in the darkest shade and State P in the lightest
questions.B: State R in the darkest shade and State Q in the lightest
questions.C: all four states in exactly the same shade of grey
questions.D: State P in the darkest shade and State S in the lightest
questions.explanation: Choropleth shading gets darker as density increases: P (2,500) darkest, S (50) lightest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The official counting of the people of a country at a particular time is called a
questions.explanation: A census records the number, age, sex, occupation and other details of everyone in a country, usually every ten years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's last national population census was conducted in
questions.explanation: The 2006 census gave a figure of about 140 million; the census planned for 2023 was postponed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The number of live births per 1,000 people in a year is the
questions.explanation: Crude birth rate = (births ÷ total population) × 1,000.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate of a country is its
questions.explanation: Natural increase ignores migration; total growth = natural increase + net migration.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A population pyramid with a very broad base and a narrow top indicates
questions.A: a low birth rate and long life expectancy
questions.C: a high birth rate and a high proportion of young people
questions.explanation: Such pyramids are typical of developing countries like Nigeria, where about 40% of the people are under 15.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The dependency ratio of a country is the ratio of
questions.A: the number of males to the number of females
questions.B: the number of births to the number of deaths each year
questions.C: the people living in towns to those living in villages
questions.D: the young and the old to the working-age population
questions.explanation: Dependants (under 15 and over 64) are supported by the economically active group aged 15–64.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The number of infants who die before their first birthday per 1,000 live births is the
questions.explanation: Infant mortality is a sensitive indicator of health care, nutrition and sanitation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A country with a birth rate of 40 per thousand and a death rate of 12 per thousand has a natural increase of
questions.explanation: 40 − 12 = 28 per thousand = 2.8% per year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors encourages dense population in an area?
questions.explanation: Fertile lowlands like the Nile valley and the Kano close-settled zone support many people per square kilometre.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a physical factor affecting population distribution?
questions.explanation: Physical factors are relief, climate, soils, water supply, vegetation and minerals; the others are human factors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The most densely populated continent is
questions.explanation: Asia has about 60% of the world's people; India and China each exceed 1.4 billion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Optimum population is the population that
questions.A: is the largest number of people a country can possibly feed
questions.B: has more old people than young people and is therefore declining
questions.C: is smaller than the number the country's resources can support
questions.D: gives the highest standard of living with the available resources and technology
questions.explanation: Over-population exists when numbers exceed the optimum and under-population when they fall below it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following countries has the largest population in Africa?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's population is estimated at over 220 million, followed by Ethiopia and Egypt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The theory that population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically was put forward by
questions.explanation: Thomas Malthus (1798) predicted famine, disease and war as checks on population growth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the demographic transition model, the stage of high birth rate and rapidly falling death rate is characterised by
questions.A: slow population growth with a stable age structure
questions.B: zero growth with births equal to deaths
questions.C: population decline as deaths exceed births
questions.explanation: Improved medicine and sanitation cut deaths before birth rates fall; most of Africa is in this stage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The sex ratio of a population is the
questions.explanation: A sex ratio above 100 means more males than females; mining towns often have high sex ratios.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Life expectancy refers to the
questions.A: age at which most workers retire from active service
questions.B: age of the oldest living person in a country
questions.C: total number of people aged 65 years and above
questions.D: average number of years a newborn baby is expected to live
questions.explanation: Life expectancy in Nigeria is about 55 years compared with over 80 years in Japan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: One reason for the high birth rate in many African countries is
questions.B: high cost of living in towns
questions.C: early marriage and the desire for large families
questions.explanation: Early marriage, low female education, religious beliefs and the value of children as farm labour and old-age security keep fertility high.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Population data are useful to governments for
questions.A: planning schools, hospitals, housing and elections
questions.B: predicting the timing of earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
questions.C: measuring the amount of rainfall received each year
questions.D: drawing contour lines on topographical maps
questions.explanation: Accurate figures guide the allocation of resources, constituencies and revenue among states.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A country records 500,000 births, 200,000 deaths, 50,000 immigrants and 80,000 emigrants in a year. Its total population growth for the year is
questions.explanation: Natural increase 300,000 + net migration (50,000 − 80,000 = −30,000) = 270,000.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The movement of people from one place to another with the intention of settling is called
questions.explanation: Migration may be internal (within a country) or international, voluntary or forced.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The movement of people from villages to towns is called
questions.explanation: Rural–urban drift is the main cause of rapid city growth in developing countries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a push factor of migration?
questions.A: better job opportunities in the city
questions.B: good schools and hospitals in the city
questions.C: unemployment and poverty in the village
questions.explanation: Push factors drive people out of the source area; pull factors attract them to the destination.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A person who leaves Nigeria to settle in Canada is, from Nigeria's point of view,
questions.explanation: Emigrants leave a country; immigrants enter it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The seasonal movement of Fulani herdsmen and their cattle between wet and dry season pastures is an example of
questions.explanation: Transhumance follows the availability of pasture and water and the retreat of tsetse fly.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a consequence of rural–urban migration for the rural areas?
questions.A: shortage of farm labour and an ageing population
questions.B: overcrowding and the growth of slums and shanty towns
questions.C: traffic congestion on the roads during rush hours
questions.D: a steep rise in house rents and the cost of land
questions.explanation: The villages lose their young, energetic people, while the towns suffer overcrowding, unemployment and slums.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The loss of highly skilled professionals such as doctors from Nigeria to Europe and America is referred to as
questions.explanation: Brain drain deprives developing countries of the trained manpower needed for development, although remittances flow back.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: People forced to flee their homes because of war or persecution and who cross an international border are called
questions.explanation: Those displaced within their own country are internally displaced persons (IDPs), as in north-east Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following problems is associated with rapid population growth in developing countries?
questions.A: pressure on land, food, housing, schools and health services
questions.B: a serious shortage of labour in farms and factories
questions.C: too many old people dependent on a small workforce
questions.D: large areas of farmland abandoned for lack of farmers
questions.explanation: When growth outpaces the economy, unemployment, malnutrition and environmental degradation increase.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A policy adopted by China to control population growth was the
questions.explanation: From 1979 to 2015 most Chinese families were limited to one child; the policy has since been relaxed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a measure for controlling rapid population growth?
questions.A: early marriage of girls after primary school
questions.B: polygamy and the payment of high bride price
questions.D: banning the conduct of national censuses
questions.explanation: Educated women marry later and have fewer children; access to contraception reduces fertility.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Ravenstein laws of migration state that
questions.A: most migrants move only a short distance
questions.B: migrants always move to another continent
questions.explanation: Ravenstein also noted that long-distance migrants go to big cities, that each stream has a counter-stream and that towns grow by migration.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem of an ageing population, as in Japan and Western Europe?
questions.A: a shortage of primary and secondary schools
questions.B: too many primary-school children for the available teachers
questions.C: a very high rate of infant mortality
questions.D: a rising burden of pensions and health care on a shrinking workforce
questions.explanation: Low birth rates and long life expectancy raise the proportion of elderly dependants.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Remittances sent home by migrants benefit the source area by
questions.B: reducing the population of the destination
questions.C: providing income for families, housing and small businesses
questions.explanation: Nigeria receives over 20 billion US dollars a year in diaspora remittances.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement whose people are engaged mainly in farming, fishing, lumbering or mining is described as
questions.explanation: Rural settlements are small, with primary occupations; urban settlements have secondary and tertiary functions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The smallest type of rural settlement, consisting of a few houses, is a
questions.explanation: The hierarchy runs hamlet, village, town, city, conurbation, megalopolis.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement in which houses are grouped closely together is described as
questions.explanation: Nucleation is encouraged by a point water supply, defence needs, community farming and fertile land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The actual piece of land on which a settlement is built is its
questions.explanation: Site refers to the local physical characteristics (e.g. hill top, river bank); situation is the position relative to surrounding features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement located where a river can be crossed is called a
questions.explanation: Bridge towns such as Lokoja and Onitsha grew at river crossings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main factor that determined the location of Abuja as Nigeria's capital was
questions.A: the presence of large petroleum deposits nearby
questions.B: its high rainfall and dense forest vegetation
questions.C: its coastal site with a natural deep-water harbour
questions.D: its central location and ethnic neutrality
questions.explanation: Abuja was chosen in 1976 for its central position, accessibility, security and land availability.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors favours a dispersed settlement pattern?
questions.A: the need for defence against attack by neighbours
questions.B: a shortage of water except at a few wells and streams
questions.C: abundant water supply everywhere and large individual farm holdings
questions.D: communal farming and shared ownership of the land
questions.explanation: Where each family can obtain water and land near its own farm there is no need to cluster.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The interaction between a town and its surrounding villages is shown by
questions.A: the flow of food to the town and manufactured goods and services to the villages
questions.B: the complete absence of trade between the town and the villages
questions.C: the villages having more functions and services than the town
questions.D: the town supplying all the food eaten in the surrounding villages
questions.explanation: Villages supply food, raw materials and labour; towns supply markets, goods, education and health services.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The area surrounding a town that is served by the town and supplies it with goods and people is its
questions.explanation: The sphere of influence grows with the size and range of the functions the town offers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of a rural settlement?
questions.explanation: Rural settlements provide food and raw materials; higher-order functions belong to towns.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A dormitory settlement is one
questions.A: where most residents sleep but travel to work in a nearby city
questions.B: that specialises in the manufacture of beds and mattresses
questions.C: with no permanent residents except during the harvest
questions.D: located in a desert far from any large city
questions.explanation: Commuter towns such as Ikorodu and Mowe-Ibafo serve Lagos workers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Settlements in the Middle East traditionally cluster round
questions.explanation: In arid lands water is the decisive factor; settlements are nucleated at oases and along rivers such as the Tigris and Euphrates.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In Western Europe, most rural settlements are
questions.A: nomadic camps that move with the herds each season
questions.B: temporary fishing camps used only in the summer months
questions.C: nucleated villages of long standing with dispersed farms in enclosed areas
questions.D: clusters of huts built by shifting cultivators
questions.explanation: Historic village nucleation plus later dispersal after land enclosure characterise the European countryside.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement built at a natural break in a ridge or line of hills is a
questions.explanation: Gap towns grow where a break in a ridge concentrates roads and railways; Lincoln and Guildford in England are classic examples.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Urbanisation refers to
questions.A: the movement of people out of the towns back to the villages
questions.B: the growth of villages into hamlets and farmsteads
questions.C: the increase in the proportion of a country's population living in towns and cities
questions.D: the decline of manufacturing industries in the cities
questions.explanation: Nigeria's urban population rose from about 10% in 1950 to over 50% today.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main cause of rapid urbanisation in developing countries is
questions.D: rural–urban migration combined with natural increase
questions.explanation: Migrants attracted by jobs and services swell cities already growing by natural increase.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The central business district (CBD) of a city is characterised by
questions.A: farms, forests and open grazing land
questions.B: low-density housing with large gardens and quiet streets
questions.C: the highest land values, tall buildings, banks, shops and offices
questions.D: heavy industries, quarries and refuse dumps
questions.explanation: Accessibility makes the city centre the most sought-after and expensive land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a problem of Nigerian cities?
questions.B: shortage of housing and growth of slums
questions.explanation: Water supply is inadequate in most Nigerian cities; congestion, slums, crime, flooding and refuse are common problems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Slums and shanty towns such as Makoko in Lagos develop because
questions.A: the rich prefer to live in them close to the lagoon
questions.B: they are close to the farms where the residents work
questions.C: the government builds them to house civil servants
questions.D: migrants cannot afford decent housing and settle on marginal land
questions.explanation: Poor migrants build makeshift homes on swamps, river banks and hillsides without services.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The merging of several towns into one continuous built-up area is called a
questions.explanation: Lagos–Ikeja–Ikorodu and the Ruhr in Germany are conurbations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A city whose population is many times that of the next largest city in the country is called a
questions.explanation: Lagos, Accra and Dakar dominate their national urban systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a solution to urban traffic congestion?
questions.A: building more houses and offices in the CBD
questions.B: closing all markets located along major roads
questions.C: banning bicycles and motorcycles from the city
questions.D: developing mass transit systems such as BRT and light rail
questions.explanation: Lagos BRT and the Blue and Red rail lines aim to move more people in fewer vehicles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The growth of towns outward into the surrounding countryside is called
questions.explanation: Sprawl consumes farmland and increases journey times and infrastructure costs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Satellite towns are built in order to
questions.A: attract tourists and holiday-makers to the countryside
questions.B: increase the crime rate and overcrowding in the large city
questions.C: relieve congestion in a large city with nearby housing and jobs
questions.D: replace the villages destroyed by floods and erosion
questions.explanation: Examples include the satellite towns of the Federal Capital Territory such as Kubwa and Gwagwalada.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following functions is characteristic of Lagos but NOT of Kano?
questions.explanation: Lagos is a coastal port; Kano, an inland city, is a commercial, industrial and administrative centre.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The problem of flooding in Lagos is worsened by
questions.A: the high altitude of the city above the level of the sea
questions.B: the dry Harmattan winds blowing from the Sahara desert
questions.C: blocked drains and building on low-lying wetlands
questions.D: the absence of rainfall for most months of the year
questions.explanation: Refuse in drains, reclamation of swamps and heavy rain produce frequent floods in Victoria Island, Lekki and Ajegunle.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Urban renewal refers to
questions.C: the migration of people to villages
questions.D: the redevelopment of decayed parts of a city
questions.explanation: Slum clearance and rebuilding, as attempted at Maroko and Isale Eko, are forms of urban renewal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Farming in which almost all the produce is consumed by the farmer's family is called
questions.explanation: Small scattered plots, simple tools and mixed crops characterise subsistence farming in West Africa.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A farming system in which a plot is cultivated for a few years and then abandoned for a new plot while the old one regains fertility is
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation (bush fallowing when the settlement is permanent) is sustainable only where population is sparse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of shifting cultivation?
questions.A: it conserves the soil and protects the forest from fire
questions.B: it requires large capital and highly skilled labour
questions.C: it uses heavy machinery that compacts and damages the soil
questions.D: it wastes land, destroys forest and cannot feed many people
questions.explanation: As population grows the fallow period shortens and soil fertility declines.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Plantation agriculture is characterised by
questions.A: small scattered plots growing a mixture of food crops for the family
questions.B: nomadic herding of cattle and goats over open grassland
questions.C: large estates growing a single cash crop for export with hired labour and scientific methods
questions.D: cultivation only during the annual floods of a large river
questions.explanation: Rubber, oil palm, tea, coffee, cocoa and sugar cane are plantation crops.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The keeping of animals and growing of crops on the same farm is known as
questions.explanation: Crops feed the animals and animal manure fertilises the fields, as in Western Europe.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Intensive cultivation of vegetables, fruits and flowers near large cities for sale is called
questions.explanation: Perishable produce is grown close to the urban market, e.g. around Lagos, Jos and Kano.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nomadic herding is practised mainly in
questions.B: densely populated river valleys and deltas
questions.C: semi-arid grasslands such as the Sahel and Central Asia
questions.D: the tundra of the Arctic only
questions.explanation: The Fulani, Tuareg and Masai move their herds in search of pasture and water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The large-scale rearing of cattle on extensive grasslands in the USA, Argentina and Australia is called
questions.explanation: Ranches cover thousands of hectares with a low density of animals and workers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem of agriculture in tropical Africa?
questions.A: excess capital and too much farm machinery on small farms
questions.B: too much mechanisation of the small family farms
questions.C: pests, poor storage, land tenure and inadequate credit
questions.D: over-supply of fertiliser and improved seeds to farmers
questions.explanation: Low yields result from these constraints together with erratic rainfall and poor transport.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Irrigation farming is most necessary in
questions.D: arid and semi-arid regions and during the dry season
questions.explanation: Schemes such as Bakolori (Sokoto), South Chad and Kano River supply water where rain is inadequate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The green revolution refers to
questions.A: the planting of belts of trees to halt the advance of the desert
questions.B: the spread of forests over abandoned farmland
questions.C: the increase in food output through high-yielding seed varieties, fertilisers and irrigation
questions.D: the growth of grasslands after the clearing of forest
questions.explanation: It transformed wheat and rice output in India, Mexico and the Philippines from the 1960s.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a factor affecting agriculture?
questions.explanation: Physical factors (climate, soil, relief, drainage) and human factors (labour, capital, markets, technology, government policy) determine farming.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Dairy farming is highly developed in Denmark and the Netherlands because of
questions.A: hot dry climates that keep the cattle free of disease
questions.B: poor transport that keeps milk prices high
questions.C: the absence of towns and factories in the countryside
questions.D: cool moist climates that produce good pasture, near large urban markets
questions.explanation: Lush grass, skilled farmers, cooperatives and nearby markets make north-west Europe a leading dairy region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lumbering in the tropical rainforest is difficult because
questions.A: the trees grow in pure stands of a single species
questions.B: there are no rivers along which the logs can be floated
questions.C: valuable species are scattered among many other species and the wood is heavy
questions.D: the trees are too small to be worth cutting
questions.explanation: Compared with coniferous forests, tropical hardwoods are dispersed, heavy (they may not float) and hard to reach.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The world's leading producer of cocoa is
questions.explanation: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana together supply over half of world cocoa; Nigeria ranks about fourth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Wet (paddy) rice cultivation in monsoon Asia is characterised by
questions.A: extensive mechanised farms with very few workers
questions.B: nomadic herding combined with occasional cropping
questions.C: intensive cultivation of small flooded plots with much labour
questions.D: plantation estates owned by large foreign companies
questions.explanation: High temperatures, heavy rain, flat alluvial land and dense population support intensive subsistence rice farming.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Fishing is well developed on the continental shelves of the North Atlantic because
questions.A: the water is very deep and cold throughout the year
questions.B: the sea is frozen for most of the year
questions.C: there are no ports along the coasts of the neighbouring countries
questions.D: shallow water, plankton and the meeting of warm and cold currents favour fish
questions.explanation: The Grand Banks of Newfoundland and the North Sea are famous fishing grounds for these reasons.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The method of mining used when the mineral lies close to the surface is
questions.explanation: Open-cast (open-pit) mining strips off the overburden; it is used for tin on the Jos Plateau and limestone at Ewekoro.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Alluvial (placer) mining is used to obtain
questions.D: tin and gold from river gravels
questions.explanation: Loose deposits in stream beds are washed or dredged to separate the heavy mineral.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Petroleum is obtained by
questions.explanation: Wells are drilled through overlying rock into the oil-bearing strata, on land or offshore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main factor that determines whether a mineral deposit is worked is
questions.A: the colour and hardness of the mineral
questions.B: the distance of the deposit from the equator
questions.C: the cost of extraction relative to the value of the mineral
questions.D: the age of the rocks that contain the mineral
questions.explanation: Size and grade of the deposit, depth, accessibility, transport, labour, capital and market prices all affect profitability.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: HEP, solar, wind, tidal, geothermal and biomass are renewable; fossil fuels are not.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Hydro-electric power generation requires
questions.A: flat land, a dry climate and a plentiful supply of coal
questions.B: a large volume of fast-flowing water, a suitable dam site and a market for the power
questions.C: large coal deposits close to a navigable river
questions.D: warm ocean currents flowing along a rocky coast
questions.explanation: Kainji, Jebba and Shiroro on the Niger and Kaduna rivers meet these conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following countries is a leading producer of petroleum?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia, the USA, Russia, Iraq and Iran are among the top producers; Nigeria leads in Africa.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Coal is important to industry mainly as a source of
questions.D: energy and coke for iron smelting
questions.explanation: Coking coal is essential for blast furnaces; coal also fuels thermal power stations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Solar energy is most abundant in
questions.A: the polar regions during the long winter night
questions.B: hot deserts and savanna regions with many hours of sunshine
questions.C: equatorial regions with heavy cloud cover all year
questions.D: cool temperate regions with frequent depressions
questions.explanation: Northern Nigeria receives over 3,000 hours of sunshine a year, ideal for solar power.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) aims to
questions.A: reduce the oil production of its members to zero
questions.B: distribute free crude oil to the poorest countries
questions.C: coordinate the petroleum policies of members and stabilise prices
questions.D: control the price of gold on the world market
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined OPEC in 1971; members agree production quotas to influence world prices.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: One negative effect of mining on the environment is
questions.A: improved soil fertility around the mines
questions.B: reduced flooding in the surrounding valleys
questions.C: increased forest cover on the mined land
questions.D: land degradation, water pollution and abandoned mine ponds
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau tin fields are scarred with mine ponds and derelict land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Natural gas is mainly used for
questions.B: power generation, cooking fuel and industrial feedstock
questions.explanation: Nigeria's LNG plant at Bonny exports liquefied gas and gas fuels most thermal power stations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Thermal power stations generate electricity by
questions.A: using water falling from a high dam
questions.B: using the rise and fall of the tides
questions.C: burning fuel to produce steam that drives turbines
questions.D: using the fusion of hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: Egbin near Lagos and Afam in Rivers State burn natural gas; coal-fired stations are common in China and India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nuclear power is generated in countries such as France and the USA using
questions.explanation: Fission of uranium releases heat that produces steam; waste disposal and accidents are major concerns.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Industries that process raw materials directly from farms, forests and mines are called
questions.explanation: Manufacturing (secondary) converts primary products into finished goods; primary industries extract them.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a factor influencing the location of industries?
questions.A: the words of the national anthem and the national pledge
questions.B: nearness to raw materials, power, labour, market and transport
questions.C: the phase of the moon at the time the factory is built
questions.D: the colour of the soil on which the factory stands
questions.explanation: Capital, water, government policy and personal choice also matter.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Industries that lose weight during manufacture, such as cement and sugar refining, are usually located
questions.A: near the market for the product
questions.C: near the source of raw materials
questions.D: on the tops of hills and mountains
questions.explanation: It is cheaper to transport the lighter finished product than the bulky raw material.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Industries whose products are bulky, fragile or perishable, such as bread and soft drinks, are usually located
questions.explanation: Market-oriented industries save on distribution costs and reach consumers quickly.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Heavy industry is characterised by
questions.A: small light products such as watches, radios and computers
questions.B: bulky raw materials and products, large sites and heavy machinery, e.g. iron and steel
questions.C: handicraft production using simple tools and family labour
questions.D: work carried out at home by women and children
questions.explanation: Iron and steel, ship-building and heavy chemicals are heavy industries; electronics and textiles are light.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Cottage industries are those
questions.A: carried out in large factories with modern machinery
questions.B: located only in the largest cities of a country
questions.C: carried out in homes with simple tools and family labour
questions.D: that make cotton cloth and nothing else
questions.explanation: Weaving, pottery, leather work and blacksmithing are traditional cottage industries in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of industrialisation?
questions.A: rising unemployment in the towns and cities
questions.B: depopulation of the rural areas and villages
questions.C: pollution of the air, rivers and farmland
questions.D: creation of jobs and value added to raw materials
questions.explanation: Industry also earns foreign exchange, diversifies the economy and stimulates other sectors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The concentration of many industries in one area, sharing services and labour, is called
questions.explanation: Agglomeration economies attract new firms to existing industrial estates such as Ikeja and Trans-Amadi.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A footloose industry is one that
questions.A: must be located close to its raw materials
questions.B: is always located on the coast near a port
questions.C: can locate almost anywhere because transport costs are small
questions.D: has no workers and is fully automated
questions.explanation: Electronics, software and light assembly industries are footloose.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Ruhr region of Germany developed as a major industrial area because of
questions.A: its warm sunny climate and fertile agricultural soils
questions.B: its extensive deserts and deposits of mineral salts
questions.C: the large number of tourists who visit the region each year
questions.D: rich coalfields, iron ore, the Rhine waterway and a large market
questions.explanation: Coal and navigable rivers were the classic basis of European heavy industry.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Japan is a leading industrial nation despite few raw materials because of
questions.A: its large deserts which supply cheap sand for glass making
questions.B: skilled labour, technology, capital, good ports and imported raw materials
questions.C: its hot climate which allows factories to work all year
questions.D: its isolation from all other industrial countries
questions.explanation: Japan imports iron ore, oil and coal and exports high-value manufactured goods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: One major problem facing manufacturing industries in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Firms spend heavily on generators; poor infrastructure, smuggling and forex shortages add to costs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Industries that make goods used by other industries, such as machinery and steel, are called
questions.explanation: Capital goods produce the means of production; consumer goods are for final use.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The iron and steel industry is usually located near
questions.B: coal, iron ore or a port through which they are imported
questions.explanation: Ajaokuta was sited near Itakpe iron ore and the Niger; Aladja depends on imported ore through Warri.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The cheapest means of transporting bulky goods over long distances is
questions.explanation: Ships carry huge cargoes at low cost per tonne, although slowly.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The fastest but most expensive mode of transport is
questions.explanation: Air transport suits passengers, mail and light valuable or perishable goods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An advantage of road transport over rail transport is that it
questions.B: is cheaper for heavy bulky goods over long distances
questions.explanation: Roads reach places railways cannot and allow easy loading and unloading.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Pipelines are used mainly to transport
questions.C: crude oil, refined products, gas and water
questions.explanation: Pipelines link the Niger Delta oil fields to refineries and depots across Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The River Niger is not fully navigable throughout the year because of
questions.A: its very great length from source to mouth
questions.B: the many bridges that have been built across it
questions.C: the crocodiles and hippos found in its waters
questions.D: rapids, sand bars and seasonal changes in water level
questions.explanation: Rapids at Jebba and Bussa and low dry-season levels restrict navigation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Suez Canal is important because it
questions.A: links the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean
questions.B: shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia by avoiding the Cape
questions.C: joins the River Niger with the River Nile
questions.D: connects the ports of Lagos and Accra
questions.explanation: The canal joins the Mediterranean and the Red Sea; the Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Trans-Siberian railway, the world's longest, is located in
questions.explanation: It runs about 9,300 km from Moscow to Vladivostok.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem of transport in tropical Africa?
questions.A: too many railways competing for the same traffic
questions.B: too many sea ports along the coasts of the region
questions.C: an excess of capital for building roads and bridges
questions.D: poor road maintenance, rugged relief, forest and flooding
questions.explanation: Colonial railways ran only from the interior to the coast, and roads deteriorate rapidly in the rains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The great circle route is important in air transport because it
questions.A: is the longest and most scenic route between two airports
questions.B: is the shortest distance between two points on the earth's surface
questions.C: avoids flying over all oceans and seas
questions.D: follows the line of the equator round the earth
questions.explanation: Aircraft between Europe and North America follow great circle routes near the Arctic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a modern means of communication?
questions.A: the town crier with a gong
questions.explanation: GSM networks and the internet have transformed business and social life in Nigeria since 2001.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Transport contributes to economic development by
questions.A: isolating regions and communities from one another
questions.B: increasing the cost of goods to the final consumers
questions.C: preventing trade between regions of a country
questions.D: linking producers with markets and opening up new areas
questions.explanation: Good transport widens markets, lowers costs, creates jobs and promotes national unity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The St Lawrence Seaway is important to North America because it
questions.A: lets ocean ships sail from the Atlantic into the Great Lakes
questions.B: connects the USA with Mexico across the Rio Grande
questions.C: is the longest railway on the continent of North America
questions.D: joins the Mississippi River to the Pacific Ocean
questions.explanation: Opened in 1959, it carries grain, iron ore and manufactured goods between the interior and the ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lagos–Ibadan standard-gauge railway and the Abuja–Kaduna line are examples of
questions.A: recent rail modernisation projects in Nigeria
questions.D: inland waterways dredged for barge traffic
questions.explanation: New standard-gauge lines (opened 2016 and 2021) are gradually replacing the old narrow-gauge network.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which port handles the largest share of Nigeria's imports?
questions.D: Baro river port in Niger State
questions.explanation: The Lagos ports handle over 70% of the country's container traffic, causing severe congestion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The exchange of goods and services between countries is called
questions.explanation: International trade involves exports and imports, currencies and customs duties.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports is its
questions.explanation: A favourable balance exists when exports exceed imports; the balance of payments also includes services and capital.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Developing countries mainly export
questions.C: primary products such as crude oil, cocoa and minerals
questions.explanation: Dependence on a few primary exports with unstable prices is a major problem of developing economies.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors promotes international trade?
questions.A: differences in natural resources, climate and technology between countries
questions.B: identical resources and technology in every country
questions.C: high tariffs and import quotas in all countries
questions.D: wars and border closures between neighbours
questions.explanation: Countries trade because they cannot produce everything they need efficiently.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A tax imposed on imported goods is called
questions.explanation: Tariffs raise revenue and protect local industries; quotas limit quantities.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's main trading partners for imports include
questions.A: China, India, the USA and the Netherlands
questions.explanation: China is the largest source of Nigeria's imports; India and Spain are major buyers of its crude oil.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Tourism is regarded as an invisible export because
questions.A: tourists cannot be seen when they enter the country
questions.B: it earns foreign exchange without goods leaving the country
questions.C: it is illegal in most countries
questions.D: it involves the smuggling of goods
questions.explanation: Foreign visitors pay for services (hotels, transport, food) with foreign currency.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a tourist attraction in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Others include Obudu Mountain Resort, Olumo Rock, Zuma Rock, Ikogosi Warm Springs, Osun-Osogbo Grove and the Argungu fishing festival.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors hinders the growth of tourism in Nigeria?
questions.C: insecurity, poor infrastructure and inadequate publicity
questions.D: a warm climate throughout the year
questions.explanation: Kidnapping, bad roads, poor hotels and visa problems discourage international visitors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) aims to
questions.A: stop all international trade in primary products
questions.B: control the weather in trading nations
questions.D: promote free trade by reducing tariffs and settling trade disputes
questions.explanation: The WTO succeeded GATT in 1995; Nigeria is a member.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Deteriorating terms of trade for a developing country means that
questions.A: it must export more to buy the same quantity of imports
questions.B: its export prices rise faster than import prices
questions.explanation: When primary product prices fall relative to manufactured imports, purchasing power of exports declines.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Ecotourism refers to tourism that
questions.A: destroys the natural environment of the host area
questions.B: takes place only in large cities and shopping malls
questions.C: is based on natural areas and conserves them for local benefit
questions.D: involves shopping for goods in duty-free shops
questions.explanation: Game reserves, forests and waterfalls attract ecotourists whose fees support conservation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main advantage of tourism to a country is
questions.A: increased pollution of beaches, rivers and forests
questions.B: rising prices of food, housing and transport
questions.C: loss of local culture, customs and traditions
questions.D: foreign exchange earnings, jobs and infrastructure
questions.explanation: Countries such as Kenya, Egypt and Spain earn large sums from visitors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria lies approximately between latitudes
questions.explanation: The country extends from about 4°N at the coast to 14°N in the far north, and from 3°E to 15°E.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria shares its western border with
questions.explanation: Benin lies to the west, Niger to the north, Chad to the north-east and Cameroon to the east.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The total land area of Nigeria is approximately
questions.explanation: Nigeria covers about 923,768 km², roughly the size of France and the UK combined.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The highest point in Nigeria, Chappal Waddi, is located on the
questions.explanation: Chappal Waddi (about 2,419 m) is in the Gashaka-Gumti area of the Mambilla Plateau, Taraba State.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Jos Plateau is important to Nigeria as
questions.A: the main coal field and source of coke for industry
questions.B: the main sea port serving the whole of northern Nigeria
questions.C: the largest oil and gas field in the whole country
questions.D: a source of tin and columbite and a major watershed
questions.explanation: Rivers such as the Kaduna, Gongola and Hadejia rise on the plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The two largest rivers in Nigeria are the
questions.explanation: They meet at Lokoja and flow south as the lower Niger to the Atlantic through the delta.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The River Niger enters Nigeria from
questions.explanation: Rising in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea, the Niger enters Nigeria at its north-western border with Benin.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The River Benue rises in
questions.A: the Jos Plateau of central Nigeria
questions.D: the Sokoto plains of the north-west
questions.explanation: The Benue flows west from Cameroon to join the Niger at Lokoja.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rivers such as the Hadejia and Yobe drain into
questions.explanation: The Chad Basin is an area of inland drainage with no outlet to the sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Niger Delta covers an area of about
questions.explanation: The delta, about 70,000 km², is one of the largest in the world and the centre of Nigeria's oil industry.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following relief regions of Nigeria lies below 300 m?
questions.A: the Sokoto plains and the coastal lowlands
questions.B: the Jos Plateau and its surrounding hills
questions.C: the Mambilla Plateau in Taraba State
questions.D: the Eastern highlands along the Cameroon border
questions.explanation: Lowlands (below 300 m) include the coastal plains, the Niger–Benue trough, the Sokoto plains and the Chad Basin.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Udi–Nsukka escarpment is located in
questions.explanation: The Udi hills, rising over 300 m, contain Nigeria's coal deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sokoto–Rima basin differs from the Basement Complex areas of Nigeria in that it
questions.A: is built of ancient crystalline rocks such as granite and gneiss
questions.B: rises above 1,500 m with a cool montane climate
questions.C: has active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes
questions.D: consists of young sedimentary rocks and has an extensive floodplain (fadama)
questions.explanation: Sedimentary basins (Sokoto, Chad, Niger–Benue trough, Niger Delta) contrast with the crystalline plateaux.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Kainji, Jebba and Shiroro dams are located on which rivers respectively?
questions.explanation: Kainji and Jebba are on the Niger; Shiroro is on the Kaduna, a Niger tributary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's coastline on the Gulf of Guinea is about
questions.explanation: The coast stretches roughly 853 km from Badagry to the Cross River estuary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's two main seasons are
questions.C: the rainy season and the dry season
questions.explanation: Rains come with the south-west monsoon; the dry season brings the north-east Harmattan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following Nigerian towns has the highest annual rainfall?
questions.explanation: Calabar and the Niger Delta receive over 3,000 mm a year; Maiduguri gets under 600 mm.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The rainy season in northern Nigeria lasts roughly from
questions.explanation: The ITD reaches the far north only in mid-year, so the wet season is short (about four months).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The mean annual temperature range is greatest in
questions.explanation: Continental interior stations have hot pre-rain months (40 °C+) and cool Harmattan nights, giving large ranges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vegetation belt found along the coast of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Salt-water mangroves fringe the lagoons and delta creeks, with freshwater swamp forest inland.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vegetation belt found in the extreme north-east of Nigeria near Lake Chad is the
questions.explanation: The Sahel has short grasses, thorny acacia and rainfall below 600 mm.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Arranged from south to north, Nigeria's vegetation belts are
questions.A: Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna, rainforest, swamp forest
questions.B: swamp forest, rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
questions.C: rainforest, Sahel savanna, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, swamp forest
questions.D: Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna, rainforest, swamp forest
questions.explanation: The belts run in west–east bands that become drier northwards with decreasing rainfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Cocoa cultivation is concentrated in the rainforest belt of south-western Nigeria because
questions.A: of the long dry season and low humidity of the area
questions.B: of heavy well-distributed rainfall, high humidity and deep well-drained soils
questions.C: of the sandy desert soils and strong winds of the area
questions.D: of the low temperatures and frequent frost of the area
questions.explanation: Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Ekiti and Cross River states are the main cocoa producers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The soils of the Nigerian rainforest belt are generally
questions.A: very fertile because of the heavy rainfall
questions.B: heavily leached, acidic and low in nutrients once cleared
questions.C: black cotton soils rich in humus
questions.D: rich in lime from underlying chalk
questions.explanation: Nutrients are held in the vegetation and are quickly lost when the forest is cleared.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Harmattan season in Nigeria is characterised by
questions.B: dry dusty haze, low humidity and cool nights
questions.C: hot humid nights and heavy dew
questions.D: strong sea breezes and high humidity
questions.explanation: Visibility falls, lips crack and airports sometimes close because of the dust.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Southern Nigeria has a double maximum of rainfall because
questions.A: it is drained by two large rivers and their tributaries
questions.B: the ITD passes over it twice a year, going north then south
questions.C: of the dry Harmattan winds blowing from the Sahara
questions.D: of its altitude above the level of the sea
questions.explanation: Peaks occur around June–July and September, separated by the August break.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Guinea savanna of Nigeria is important for the cultivation of
questions.B: yam, guinea corn, maize and rice
questions.explanation: The Middle Belt is Nigeria's main producer of root crops and cereals.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following climatic hazards affects northern Nigeria most?
questions.explanation: Unreliable rainfall in the Sahel produces recurrent drought.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The most populous state in Nigeria according to the 2006 census was
questions.explanation: Kano recorded about 9.4 million, slightly more than Lagos (9.0 million), though Lagos disputed the figures.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following areas of Nigeria is sparsely populated?
questions.A: the Igbo heartland of the south-eastern states
questions.B: the Middle Belt (e.g. parts of Niger, Kwara and Taraba)
questions.C: the Kano close-settled zone of the north
questions.D: the Lagos metropolitan area of the south-west
questions.explanation: Historical slave raids, tsetse fly, poor soils and rugged relief left the Middle Belt thinly peopled.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The high population density of the Kano close-settled zone is due to
questions.A: large petroleum deposits under the surrounding farmland
questions.B: fertile soils, long intensive farming and Kano's commerce
questions.C: heavy rainfall throughout the year and dense forest cover
questions.D: its coastal location and its large fishing industry
questions.explanation: Manure from the city and irrigation of fadama land support continuous cultivation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The high population density of south-eastern Nigeria is associated with
questions.A: large-scale mining of tin, coal and columbite
questions.B: fertile soils, early settlement and high fertility
questions.C: large irrigation schemes on the river flood plains
questions.D: desert conditions and the nomadic herding of cattle
questions.explanation: Land pressure has produced serious soil erosion and out-migration to other parts of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's population is estimated to be growing at about
questions.explanation: At this rate the population doubles in roughly 28 years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The three most numerous ethnic groups in Nigeria are the
questions.explanation: Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups; the Hausa-Fulani dominate the north, the Yoruba the south-west and the Igbo the south-east.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem created by Nigeria's rapid population growth?
questions.A: an excess of food supply over demand
questions.B: pressure on schools, hospitals, housing and jobs
questions.C: a shortage of children in the schools
questions.explanation: Public services cannot expand as fast as the population.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Population censuses in Nigeria have been controversial mainly because
questions.A: the weather is too hot for counting people in the field
questions.B: the figures are used to share revenue and political seats
questions.C: there are too few people to count accurately
questions.D: counting the population of the country is very easy
questions.explanation: Inflated counts in 1962/63 and disputes over 1991 and 2006 arose from political and financial stakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Traditional settlements in Yorubaland are noted for being
questions.A: dispersed homesteads scattered over the farmland
questions.B: large nucleated towns with the Oba's palace and market at the centre
questions.C: nomadic camps that move each season
questions.D: linear fishing villages along the lagoons only
questions.explanation: Ibadan, Ogbomoso and Oyo were large walled towns long before colonial rule.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Traditional Tiv settlements of Benue State are typically
questions.A: dispersed compounds scattered over the farmland
questions.B: large walled cities with a central palace
questions.C: coastal ports built round natural harbours
questions.D: hill forts built for defence on rocky outcrops
questions.explanation: Each compound stands within its own farmland; nucleated towns are recent.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main direction of internal migration in Nigeria is
questions.A: from the large cities back to the rural villages
questions.B: from rural areas and the north to the southern cities
questions.C: from Lagos northwards to the Sahel and Lake Chad
questions.D: from the coast to the shores of Lake Chad
questions.explanation: Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt and Kano attract migrants from all parts of the country.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Groundnuts, cotton and millet are produced mainly in
questions.explanation: The Sudan savanna's long sunny season and sandy soils suit these crops.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Oil palm, rubber and cocoa are produced mainly in the
questions.explanation: These tree crops need heavy rainfall and high humidity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main cattle-rearing area of Nigeria is the
questions.A: rainforest belt of the southern states
questions.B: northern savanna, largely free of tsetse fly
questions.C: Niger Delta and its many creeks
questions.explanation: Trypanosomiasis carried by tsetse restricts cattle in the humid south; over 90% of cattle are in the north.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Fulani herdsmen move their cattle southwards during the dry season because
questions.A: there is more tsetse in the north
questions.B: pasture and water become scarce in the north
questions.explanation: This transhumance has increasingly led to farmer–herder conflict in the Middle Belt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem of agriculture in Nigeria?
questions.A: excessive mechanisation of the small family farms
questions.B: land tenure, poor storage and low use of improved inputs
questions.C: over-supply of credit to small-scale farmers
questions.D: too many extension workers for each farmer
questions.explanation: Fragmented holdings and ageing farmers limit output; post-harvest losses reach 40% for some crops.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Kano River Project and the Bakolori Project are examples of
questions.explanation: River basin development authorities built dams for dry-season irrigation of wheat, rice and vegetables.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria is the world's largest producer of
questions.explanation: Nigeria produces about 60 million tonnes of cassava a year and about two-thirds of the world's yams.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rice is grown extensively in the fadama (floodplain) areas of
questions.B: Kebbi, Niger, Ebonyi and Benue states
questions.explanation: Kebbi (Argungu, Birnin Kebbi) and Ebonyi (Abakaliki) are major rice producers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Fishing in Nigeria is carried out mainly in
questions.A: the sand dunes of the Sahara
questions.B: coastal waters, lagoons, rivers and lakes such as Kainji and Chad
questions.C: the rocky streams of the Jos Plateau
questions.D: mountain streams of the Mambilla Plateau only
questions.explanation: Artisanal fishermen supply most of the catch; fish farming (aquaculture) is growing rapidly.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The decline of Nigeria's agricultural exports after 1970 was mainly due to
questions.A: climate change and the shrinking of Lake Chad alone
questions.B: the oil boom, which drew labour and investment away from farming
questions.C: the abolition of the marketing boards in the year 1900
questions.D: a fall in world population and demand for food
questions.explanation: Petroleum revenue overvalued the naira and neglected agriculture; groundnut pyramids and palm-oil exports disappeared.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Kola nut is produced mainly in
questions.explanation: Kola is grown in the forest belt and traded to the north where it is widely consumed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following crops is grown mainly in the Middle Belt of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Benue, Nasarawa, Kogi and Niger states lead in yam, benniseed and soya bean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Agricultural extension services are meant to
questions.A: collect taxes and levies from farmers
questions.B: teach farmers improved methods and inputs
questions.explanation: The Agricultural Development Projects (ADPs) in each state run extension programmes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's most important mineral export is
questions.explanation: Petroleum and gas provide about 90% of export earnings and over half of government revenue.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Coal is mined in Nigeria at
questions.explanation: Enugu's coal mines, opened in 1915, gave the city the name 'Coal City'; Okaba in Kogi also has coal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Tin and columbite are mined mainly on the
questions.explanation: Alluvial and open-cast mining on the Jos Plateau has left many mine ponds around Jos and Bukuru.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Limestone, used in the cement industry, is quarried at
questions.explanation: Cement factories are located near these limestone deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Iron ore for the Ajaokuta steel complex was to come from
questions.explanation: The Itakpe deposit, about 60 km from Ajaokuta, is linked by rail to the steel plant.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's main oil-producing states include
questions.B: Rivers, Delta, Akwa Ibom and Bayelsa
questions.explanation: Oil fields are concentrated in the Niger Delta and offshore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's petroleum refineries are located at
questions.explanation: The state refineries have long operated below capacity; the private Dangote refinery at Lekki opened in 2024.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Kainji Dam on the River Niger was completed in
questions.explanation: Kainji (1968) was Nigeria's first major HEP project; Jebba followed in 1985 and Shiroro in 1990.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Most of Nigeria's electricity is generated from
questions.A: coal mined at Enugu and Okaba in Kogi State
questions.B: gas-fired thermal stations plus hydro-electric dams
questions.C: nuclear energy from imported uranium fuel rods
questions.D: wind farms built along the Atlantic coastline
questions.explanation: Gas-fired plants such as Egbin, Afam and Olorunsogo supply the bulk; HEP comes from Kainji, Jebba and Shiroro.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main industrial centres of Nigeria are
questions.A: Lagos, Kano, Kaduna, Port Harcourt and Aba
questions.explanation: These centres have markets, labour, power and transport; Lagos alone has over half of the country's manufacturing.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Textile industries developed in Kaduna and Kano because of
questions.A: nearness to the sea and the ports of Lagos
questions.B: local cotton supply, large markets and state investment
questions.C: large coal deposits in the surrounding area
questions.D: heavy rainfall throughout the whole year
questions.explanation: Northern cotton fed the mills, though most have since closed because of smuggling and power problems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The liquefied natural gas plant at Bonny Island is significant because it
questions.A: produces cement for the building industry
questions.B: converts gas that was formerly flared into an export product
questions.C: refines crude oil into petrol and diesel
questions.D: generates hydro-electric power for the grid
questions.explanation: NLNG makes Nigeria one of the world's leading LNG exporters and reduces gas flaring.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Aladja (Delta) steel plant was designed to use
questions.B: imported iron ore through the port of Warri
questions.C: tin ore from the Jos Plateau
questions.explanation: Aladja uses the direct-reduction process with natural gas and imported ore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following minerals is found at Azara in Nasarawa State?
questions.explanation: Barytes is used in oil drilling mud; Nasarawa is called the 'Home of Solid Minerals'.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The most widely used means of transport in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Roads carry over 90% of passengers and goods in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The colonial railway lines of Nigeria were built mainly to
questions.A: link all the state capitals with one another by rail
questions.B: carry export crops and minerals from the interior to the ports
questions.C: serve tourists visiting the game reserves of the north
questions.D: connect Nigeria with the neighbouring Cameroon and Chad
questions.explanation: Lagos–Kano (1912) and Port Harcourt–Maiduguri lines carried groundnuts, cotton, tin and coal to the coast.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's inland river ports include
questions.explanation: Inland ports on the Niger aim to relieve the Lagos ports, but shallow water limits their use.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main international airports of Nigeria are located in
questions.A: Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Port Harcourt and Enugu
questions.explanation: Murtala Muhammed (Lagos) and Nnamdi Azikiwe (Abuja) handle most international traffic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lagos–Kano trade route is important because it
questions.A: links the Sahara desert to the Atlantic coast
questions.B: connects the main port with the largest northern commercial centre
questions.C: is served by a railway line and nothing else
questions.D: carries petroleum products and nothing else
questions.explanation: Goods flow north from Lagos and farm produce and livestock flow south.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's main export by value is
questions.explanation: Non-oil exports such as cocoa, sesame, cashew and urea are a small but growing share.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria imports mainly
questions.A: crude oil, liquefied natural gas and bitumen
questions.B: machinery, vehicles, refined fuel, chemicals and food
questions.C: cocoa beans, sesame seed and raw cashew nuts
questions.D: tin ore, columbite, coal and limestone
questions.explanation: Heavy food and fuel imports reflect weak local processing capacity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A major problem of Nigeria's foreign trade is
questions.A: too many different products competing for export
questions.B: over-dependence on crude oil with its unstable price
questions.C: the absence of sea ports along the Atlantic coast
questions.D: an excess of foreign exchange earnings every year
questions.explanation: Oil price collapses in 1986, 2016 and 2020 caused recessions and currency devaluation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Lagos port is correct?
questions.A: it is located on the banks of the River Niger
questions.B: it is Nigeria's busiest port, handling most imports
questions.C: it exports mainly coal from Enugu
questions.D: it lies on the shores of Lake Chad
questions.explanation: Apapa and Tin Can Island ports, on the Lagos lagoon, dominate Nigeria's shipping.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria is divided into
questions.A: 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states, the FCT (Abuja) and 774 local government areas, grouped into six geopolitical zones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Federal Capital Territory was carved out mainly from
questions.B: the former Niger, Plateau and Kwara states
questions.explanation: The FCT lies in the geographical centre of the country; the capital moved from Lagos to Abuja in 1991.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a difference between the northern and southern parts of Nigeria?
questions.A: the north is wetter, with rainforest and tree crops, while the south is dry savanna
questions.B: the north is drier, with savanna vegetation and cereal farming, while the south is humid, forested and grows tree crops
questions.C: the south has Sahel vegetation and the north has swamp forest
questions.D: the north has mangrove swamps while the south has thorn scrub
questions.explanation: Climate explains the contrast in vegetation, crops, building materials and settlement patterns.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lagos–Badagry expressway and the Lagos–Ibadan expressway are examples of
questions.explanation: Federal trunk 'A' roads link the ports with the interior and neighbouring countries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lekki Deep Sea Port, opened in 2023, is intended to
questions.A: replace all the airports in Lagos State
questions.B: relieve congestion at Apapa and handle larger container ships
questions.C: serve the fishing communities of Lake Chad
questions.D: export coal from the mines of Enugu
questions.explanation: Lekki is Nigeria's first deep-sea port capable of berthing very large vessels.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: ECOWAS stands for
questions.A: East Central Organisation of West African States
questions.B: Economic Community of West African States
questions.C: Economic Council of West African Studies
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was founded in Lagos on 28 May 1975 by the Treaty of Lagos.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The headquarters of ECOWAS is located in
questions.explanation: The Commission moved from Lagos to Abuja; the ECOWAS Court of Justice and Parliament are also in Abuja.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: ECOWAS was established in
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed in Lagos on 28 May 1975 and revised in Cotonou in 1993.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main aim of ECOWAS is to
questions.A: form a single army for the whole of West Africa
questions.B: promote economic integration among West African states
questions.C: colonise other regions of the African continent
questions.D: control world oil prices together with OPEC
questions.explanation: Objectives include free movement of people and goods, a customs union and eventually a common currency.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of ECOWAS to member states?
questions.A: increased tariffs on goods from members
questions.B: free movement of persons and goods and a larger market
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS passport and the Trade Liberalisation Scheme aim to make the region one market.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: ECOMOG was the ECOWAS
questions.A: regional trade and development bank in Lomé
questions.B: peace-keeping force sent to Liberia and Sierra Leone
questions.C: regional airline based in Lagos and Accra
questions.D: railway company linking the West African capitals
questions.explanation: Nigeria provided most of the troops and funding for ECOMOG from 1990.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem facing ECOWAS?
questions.A: a single common language spoken by all member states
questions.B: political instability, colonial legacies and many currencies
questions.C: excess funding from the member states each year
questions.D: too few member states to form a viable market
questions.explanation: Coups, smuggling, border closures and non-payment of dues have slowed integration; Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger withdrew in 2025.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Most Francophone members of ECOWAS use the currency called the
questions.explanation: The West African CFA franc is pegged to the euro; the proposed common currency is the 'eco'.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following countries is a member of ECOWAS?
questions.explanation: Ghana, Nigeria, Benin, Togo, Côte d'Ivoire, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Senegal, Gambia and Cape Verde are members.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria plays a dominant role in ECOWAS because it
questions.A: is the smallest member in area and population
questions.B: has the largest population, economy and military in the region
questions.C: has no land borders with other members
questions.D: uses the CFA franc like the Francophone members
questions.explanation: Nigeria contributes the largest share of the budget and hosts the headquarters.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The West African Gas Pipeline carries Nigerian gas to
questions.explanation: The pipeline, fed from the Escravos–Lagos gas system, supplies power plants in the three coastal neighbours.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The country that left ECOWAS in 2000 is
questions.explanation: Mauritania withdrew in 2000 to join the Arab Maghreb Union.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Trans-West African Coastal Highway is meant to link
questions.A: Lagos with Nouakchott through the coastal states
questions.B: Abuja with Cairo across the Sahara
questions.C: Kano with Cape Town along the east coast
questions.D: Lagos with Nairobi through Central Africa
questions.explanation: The Lagos–Abidjan corridor is the busiest section of the planned highway.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following West African countries is landlocked?
questions.explanation: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger have no coastline and depend on the ports of Benin, Togo, Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal and Nigeria; the three left ECOWAS in January 2025.
